entry.title: Separate development entrypoints without moving production domain services
entry.description: An MMIS operation may begin as a diagnostic CLI and later become a production application's Query, Reader, or Linker dependency. Classify code by the production execution closure and domain responsibility, not by historical purpose or query_* filename.
applicable_when: Moving exploratory MMIS commands into a development tools area
Auditing whether query, reader, or linker modules belong in the production package
Cleaning a repository after integrating a larger MMIS orchestrator
advantages: Prevents production from depending on development tools
Avoids duplicating validated Maximo protocol and parsing logic
Keeps executable wrappers thin while preserving one formal implementation
disadvantages: Some production modules retain names associated with the earlier diagnostic operation
Requires symbol-level direct and indirect dependency analysis instead of filename-based moves
recommended_when: A production orchestrator reuses components first proven through standalone diagnostic commands
notes: Move argument parsing, stdout JSON shells, and standalone executable entrypoints to development tools.
Keep Query, Reader, Linker, transport, parser, validation, and mutation verification in production when the orchestrator directly or indirectly uses them.
Audit mixed modules at method level, but do not move a domain Reader method merely because only a diagnostic wrapper currently invokes that public capability.
Protect the boundary with an import-closure test and an inventory of every production module.
